title_si: නුවර කිරි මුහුදේ මධ්‍යම රාත්‍රී ශාපය
title_en: The Cursed Waters of Kandy Lake
location: Kandy Lake (Kiri Muhuda), Kandy District, Central Province
historical_anchor: Created in 1812 by King Sri Wickrama Rajasinghe. In May 1814, following the Ehelepola rebellion, Ehelepola Kumarihami and female relatives were forcibly drowned with heavy stones tied to their necks in the lake's deepest basin. British colonial records from 1815 onward document recurrent local reports of nocturnal weeping from Diyathilaka Mandapaya.
primary_vibe: Chilling mountain breeze across dark reflective water, damp moss on the Walakulu (cloud) wall, flickering sodium streetlights, dense fog crawling across the hills, sudden terrifying silence over the lake.
historical_sources: Historical accounts of Dr. John Davy
retention_hook_si: රෑ 12 පහු වෙලා නුවර වැව රවුමේ තනියම ඇවිදින්න එපා කියලා පැරණි මිනිස්සු කියන්නේ ඇයි කියලා ඔයා දන්නවද?
retention_hook_en: Why do locals in Sri Lanka warn travelers never to walk the shores of Kandy Lake after midnight?

title_si: බණ්ඩාරවෙල ශාන්ත තෝමස් බංගලාවේ අගුළු දැමූ කාමරය
title_en: The Sealed Room of St. Thomas' Bungalow
location: St. Thomas' Grounds, Bandarawela, Badulla District, Uva Province
historical_anchor: Erected during the late 19th-century British plantation boom. Colonial parish diaries from 1910 describe the abrupt death of a resident tea planter under unexplained psychological delirium, leading to the permanent sealing and omission of his northwest chamber from estate blueprints.
primary_vibe: Bone-chilling highland dampness, dense white mist enveloping towering eucalyptus and pine groves, creaking century-old Burma teak floorboards, distant lonely echo of the Night Mail train horn.
retention_hook_si: 1910 ඉඳන් අද වෙනකල් කිසිම කෙනෙක් ඇරියේ නැති බණ්ඩාරවෙල මේ පැරණි බංගලාවේ අගුළු දාපු කාමරය ඇතුළේ තියෙන්නේ මොනවද?
retention_hook_en: High in the mist-choked mountains of Sri Lanka stands a colonial bungalow with a room that has been padlocked shut since 1910.

title_si: යක්ෂයාගේ පඩිපෙළ සහ ඔහිය පාළු පාරේ අබිරහස
title_en: The Phantom Trail of Devil's Staircase
location: Devil's Staircase, Ohiya to Kalupahana pass, Badulla & Nuwara Eliya Border
historical_anchor: Constructed in the 1890s as a treacherous steep bridle trail for tea transport down thousand-meter precipices. Numerous laborers and horse carts plunged into the abyss. Local road registries and transport drivers have documented unexplained engine failures, phantom footsteps, and hovering marsh gas balls ('Gini Bola').
primary_vibe: Perilous sheer rock faces disappearing into bottomless abyss, swirling cold mist blinding headlights, wind howling through jagged ravines, scent of wet slate and ozone.
historical_sources: Public Works Department Ceylon Historical Reports (1895-1905)
Ceylon Railway and Transport Survey Logs
retention_hook_si: ලංකාවේ අදටත් රෑ 2 න් පස්සේ වාහනවල එන්ජින් තනියම නතර වෙන 'යක්ෂයාගේ පඩිපෙළ' පාරේ ඇත්තටම වෙන්නේ මොකක්ද?
retention_hook_en: At 2:00 AM on Sri Lanka's deadliest mountain pass, car engines stall without explanation as phantom lights dance across the precipice.

title_si: දිගම්පතහ අඳුරු වංගුව සහ මධ්‍යම රාත්‍රී කාන්තාව
location: Habarana - Dambulla Forest Highway (A6), Matale & Anuradhapura Border
historical_anchor: A 12-kilometer uninhabited jungle corridor through teak and scrub forest. Sri Lanka Police motor accident archives from the 1970s and 1980s record dozens of driver testimonies reporting a solitary woman in white standing by the asphalt before sudden catastrophic swerves.
primary_vibe: Oppressive tropical night heat pierced by sudden unnerving cold gusts, cricket and cicada buzzing abruptly cutting out, pitch-black wilderness on both sides of cracked asphalt.
historical_sources: Sri Lanka Police Traffic Investigation Archives (1976-1988)
Lanka Deepa and Daily News archival reports
retention_hook_si: දඹුල්ල සහ හබරණ අතර තියෙන මේ පාළු කැලෑ පාරේ රෑට තනියම යන රියදුරන්ට මුහුණ දෙන්න වෙන ඒ බිහිසුණු අත්දැකීම මොකක්ද?
retention_hook_en: For fifty years, night drivers on an isolated jungle highway in Sri Lanka have reported the exact same chilling roadside encounter.

title_si: රිටිගල අදටත් නොවිසඳුණු අබිරහස් සහ නොපෙනෙන භික්ෂූන්
location: Ritigala Strict Natural Reserve, North Central Province
historical_anchor: An isolated mountain range rising abruptly from the dry plains, housing 9th-century austere monasteries of the Pansukulika forest monks. Strict legal prohibition against nocturnal visitors enforced by the Department of Wildlife Conservation due to spatial disorientation, localized microclimatic inversions, and persistent claims of auditory phenomena.
primary_vibe: Ancient granite pathways covered in slippery black lichen, strange tropical microclimatic clouds hugging the canopy, absolute subterranean stillness broken by unearthly rhythmic chanting.
historical_sources: Archaeological Survey of Ceylon Annual Reports (H.C.P. Bell, 1893)
retention_hook_si: රෑ බෝ වුණාට පස්සේ ලංකාවේ කිසිම මනුස්සයෙක්ට ඇතුළු වෙන්න තහනම් රිටිගල කැලය ඇතුළේ රෑට ඇහෙන ඒ අද්භූත සද්ද මොනවද?
retention_hook_en: Sri Lanka's most protected ancient mountain is strictly forbidden after dark—and what researchers have heard echoing through its stone ruins explains why.

title_si: ගාල්ල කොටුවේ ලන්දේසි බිම්ගෙවල් සහ තාප්ප අතර හිරවූවන්
title_en: The Walled-In Souls of Galle Fort
location: Galle Dutch Fort, Galle District, Southern Province
historical_anchor: Constructed by the Portuguese (1588) and extensively fortified by the Dutch East India Company (VOC) in the 17th century. During 20th-century drainage excavations, sealed subterranean holding cells were discovered containing shackled human skeletal remains left behind by colonial military tribunals.
primary_vibe: Salty ocean spray beating against massive coral and granite ramparts, heavy scent of damp centuries-old sea salt and mildew, pitch-black gunpowder magazine corridors, mournful ocean gales.
historical_sources: Memoirs of Dutch Governors of Ceylon
retention_hook_si: ගාල්ල කොටුවේ මහ කළුගල් තාප්ප ඇතුළේ අවුරුදු 300 ක් තිස්සේ පණපිටින් හිරකරලා තිබ්බ ඒ බිහිසුණු රහස මොකක්ද?
retention_hook_en: Beneath the historic ramparts of Galle Fort lie sealed underground cells where prisoners of the Dutch Empire were buried alive.
